answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring proof of useful work over time rather than merely counting identities: each agent must complete verifiable tasks whose quality peers attest, building a reputation that is expensive to fake in bulk. Like light through a prism, one real track record refracts into many checkable signals — completed jobs, endorsements, and a history no quill can forge overnight. A newcomer starts in a shallow canyon of low trust and earns wider access only gradually, so spinning up thousands of fake agents gains nothing without months of real work.
